ranking.note: Raised from P3: correcting a wrong security threat-model explanation is the top criterion in this category, on par with the design-doc leverage of #36101.
Moved down from its score position 2: valuable internal net.h documentation, but it sits behind the privacy/security corrections and the user-facing notification docs that users hit often.
Raised from P4: it removes developer guidance that contradicts the actual codebase and has repeatedly misled logging PRs, i.e. wrong documentation rather than pure cleanup.

inconsistencies: #35858 (new doc/privacy.md, moving privacy guidance out of doc/i2p.md) and #36348 (adding -privatebroadcast notes to doc/i2p.md) touch the same text about transient vs persistent I2P identity; review #35858 first and fold #36348's correction into the consolidated page to avoid contradictory or duplicated statements.

#35480 and #35518 are both by the same author and both described as partially closing #14278 (notification behaviour). They are complementary rather than duplicates; reviewing them as a pair keeps the ZMQ and -*notify guarantees consistent with each other.
#36604 backports documentation already merged on master (#34252, #36377); its content should not be re-reviewed on the merits, only checked for correct backporting to 29.x.
result.notes: Only one clear leverage/design item (#36101) and one factual security correction (#36644) justify P2; the middle of the list is a genuinely flat P3 band of missing-documentation PRs, so position within it is driven by how often users hit the documented behaviour (privacy settings and notification scripts before internal net lifecycle notes).
